title: Sri Lankan-Style Coconut Kheema: A Creamy 350-Calorie Weeknight Dinner Fix
excerpt: Nutritionist-chef Aathira Sethumadhavan's recipe borrows from Sri Lanka's coconut gravies and Kerala's moilee and mappas, packing 22g of protein into a one-pan chicken kheema dinner with mushrooms and spinach.
body:
• Nutritionist-chef Aathira Sethumadhavan's creamy coconut kheema packs 22 grams of protein and 350 calories per serving, inspired by Sri Lankan flavors and Kerala's moilee and mappas.
  • The one-pan gravy combines chicken mince with mushrooms and spinach, served over soft chapatis or parottas, and makes three servings.
  • Key technique: simmer the coconut milk gently at the end — never let it boil hard, or it can split.
  • Watch the recipe demo in the creator's video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/3QvhJopWNaA

Weeknight dinners in diaspora kitchens often fall into a tired rotation, and nutritionist-chef Aathira Sethumadhavan has an answer for it. In an Instagram video shared on September 3, she described her creamy coconut kheema with mushrooms and spinach as "22 g protein and 350 calories per serving. Inspired by Sri Lankan flavours, Kerala style Moilee and Mappas and yet made unique with the protein and veggie choice. If your weeknight curry is getting boring, this is the fix," according to Hindustan Times.

Where the flavors come from

The recipe is a deliberate cross-cultural improvisation rather than a traditional dish. Sri Lanka's curries lean on coconut milk for body, tempered whole spices, and curry leaves for aroma. Kerala's moilee, the mild coconut-milk curry of the state's Syrian Christian kitchens, and mappas, a thicker coconut gravy, supply the creamy-gravy template. Sethumadhavan swaps in chicken mince for protein and folds in mushrooms and spinach — and for diaspora kitchens, the pantry usually already holds coconut milk and curry leaves, while the kheema replaces the longer-simmered meat of traditional curries. The result lands in under 40 minutes, which is the real point.

Ingredients (serves 3)

For the gravy:

  • 1 tbsp coconut oil (18 g)
  • Heaped ¼ tsp mustard seeds (2 g)
  • ¼ tsp fenugreek seeds (1.2 g)
  • Heaped ½ tsp fennel seeds (2 g)
  • 2-inch cinnamon stick
  • 2 sprigs curry leaves
  • ¾ cup minced onion (120 g)
  • 3 small green chillies, finely chopped (9 g)
  • 2 tsp minced garlic (9 g)
  • 1½-inch piece ginger, finely minced (9 g)
  • 1½ cups chicken mince (300 g)
  • ½ tsp turmeric powder (1.8 g)
  • ½ tsp black pepper powder (1.8 g)
  • 1½ tsp coriander powder (3.6 g)
  • 1½ tsp yellow curry powder (3.6 g)
  • Salt, to taste
  • 1½ cups diced mixed mushrooms, button and oyster (150 g)
  • 3 cups packed, chopped spinach (90 g)
  • ½ cup regular coconut milk (120 g)
  • ¾ tsp sugar (3 g)
  • A few round tomato slices (60 g)

To serve: soft chapatis or parottas

Method

  1. Heat the coconut oil in a deep pan or kadhai over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and allow them to splutter. Add the fenugreek seeds, fennel seeds, cinnamon stick and curry leaves, and sauté briefly until fragrant.
  2. Add the minced onion and chopped green chillies. Cook for a few minutes, stirring occasionally, until the onion softens and turns golden. Add the minced garlic and ginger, and sauté for another minute until aromatic.
  3. Add the chicken mince and cook over medium heat, breaking up any lumps with a spatula. Continue cooking until the mince changes colour and is cooked through.
  4. Add the turmeric, black pepper, coriander powder, yellow curry powder and some salt. Stir well to coat the chicken and cook for a couple of minutes, allowing the spices to lose their raw smell.
  5. Add the diced mushrooms and mix well. Cook until the mushrooms release their moisture and the liquid gradually reduces.
  6. Add the chopped spinach and gently fold it into the mixture. Cook until the spinach wilts and is evenly incorporated.
  7. Pour in the coconut milk and stir gently to combine. Lower the heat and simmer gently for a few minutes. Avoid bringing it to a vigorous boil, as the coconut milk may split.
  8. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Add the sugar and stir well to balance the flavors. Simmer until the gravy reaches a creamy consistency.
  9. Arrange the tomato slices over the top, cover the pan and cook for one to two minutes, until the tomatoes soften slightly.
  10. Remove from the heat and serve hot with soft chapatis or parottas.

Tips for diaspora kitchens

Use full-fat coconut milk, not the light canned version — the fat is what gives the gravy its body. If yellow curry powder is not in your spice drawer, a teaspoon of garam masala plus an extra pinch of turmeric gets close. Leftovers reheat well, though the gravy thickens in the fridge and needs a splash of water. For a vegetarian version, swap the chicken mince for crumbled tofu or an extra cup of mushrooms.

Nutrition per serving is approximately 350 kcal, 22 g protein, 12 g carbohydrates and 23 g fat, according to the Hindustan Times report — a guide for home cooking, not medical advice.
